rankings.strongest_idea: Represent every side effect as immutable effect data with stable IDs and typed receipts, leaving each domain lifecycle as a total reducer over closed ADTs.
Keep Fugue validation and routing nodes capability-free while reducers return pure transition intents executed by narrow fail-closed adapters.

rankings.fatal_flaw: The broad orchestration-runner combines persistence, publication sequencing, Fugue adaptation, and dispatch without an explicit typed effect-and-receipt protocol, leaving important orchestration behavior in an imperative component rather than fully inside the replayable functional core.
rankings.strongest_idea: Expose one typed external action from each pure domain reducer while retaining separate domain programs and a minimal shared contract.
